description: A responsive React dashboard for a college project that presents social post performance, engagement, follower growth, and scheduled posts.

services.name: Social analytics dashboard
services.features: Keep the existing React/Vite implementation and local mock JSON data. Show post performance, likes/comments/shares, follower trends, and a scheduling calendar; include reusable metric cards, charts, tables, and widgets; use React hooks, Axios, Recharts, responsive CSS Grid/Flexbox, and date-range selection; retain realistic mock data without external authentication; apply a restrained professional olive/sage/brown/beige/cream palette.

questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds static typing to the frontend.

questions.rationale: The existing application is implemented in JavaScript.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should the project use?
questions.rationale: The existing project and request specify React.

questions.question: What frontend features and requirements should be included?
questions.recommendedChoice: Retain the existing dashboard and implement the requested social analytics, scheduling, responsive layout, and visual design.
questions.answer: Keep and improve the existing React/Vite dashboard rather than replacing it. Include post performance metrics, likes/comments/shares, follower growth trends, scheduling calendar, reusable metric cards/charts/tables/widgets, React hooks and Axios, Recharts, responsive CSS Grid/Flexbox, and date range selection. Use realistic local mock data, no external authentication, and a professional restrained olive/sage/brown/beige/cream palette.
questions.rationale: These requirements are specified by the user and visible in the existing project structure.

questions.question: Which data stores does the project need?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use the existing local mock JSON data; no persistent or cloud data store is needed.

questions.rationale: The dashboard uses local mock JSON and has no persistence or file-storage requirement.

questions.question: Should users sign in to use application features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users must sign in to access application features.

options.label: No
options.description: The dashboard is available without user sign-in.

questions.rationale: The user requested realistic mock data without external authentication.
